claims.text: POL-RD-01 measures the excess as the length of the gps_trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and it is the trace, not the rounded meter copy, that governs. On this trip the recorded pickup event is the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10, while the trace runs from 18:18:40 to 18:52:12, so 2.38 km of the trace lies before the trip the platform recorded. On the assessor's own alignment figures for that artifact the segment actually driven is 20.02 km, an excess of 2.42 km, or 13.8% of the 17.6 km booked optimal - under the 20% limb of POL-RD-01. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass; the percentage limb fails, so the excess is not established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The whole-trace figures of 4.80 km and 27.3% (derived.deviation) are an artefact of counting that 2.38 km head, which is exactly why the pre-pass records that the interpretation moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

Even if the tribunal takes the whole trace as the measured trip and holds the deviation established, POL-RD-02 returns nothing to the rider. The fare model is METERED, so the recomputation runs on this trip's own figures: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP, tolls, surcharges, waiting fee and promo = 25.64, against a charged_total of 25.26. Refund = charged_total - recomputed_fare = -0.38, floored at zero; a refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis. The fare_breakdown's own derived money block carries the same result (recomputed_fare 25.6400, refund payable 0.00, below_de_minimis true). The booked optimal figures are the booking-time estimate carried on that money block; the CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT flagged on EV-TRIP-00112 (IMPAIRED, 0.4) goes to the measured actual distance, not to the booking-time optimal route or to any charged line. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge standing exactly as it is.

The reason the recomputation exceeds what was charged is visible line by line, and it is the rider's own time, not the driver's distance, that is the source. The optimal route - PIE westbound then ECP - is 17.6 km but 28.0 minutes, while the rider was charged for 20.2 minutes. The optimal-route time charge is 7.84 (28.0 x 0.28) against the 5.66 actually billed (20.2 x 0.28); that single line more than offsets the 1.80 of extra distance charge (20.0 km x 0.75 = 15.00 against 17.6 km x 0.75 = 13.20). Net of the two, the rider paid 0.38 LESS than the fare model says the optimal route would have cost.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to add on top of a zero distance-and-time refund. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll, no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount; erp_gantries is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00. No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. POL-RD-09 therefore has nothing to correct on this trip and the billing-integrity limb of POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral do not apply. The clause's test runs on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d: this driver carries 1 flag over 296 completed trips in the trailing 90 days. That is below the 3-flag limb and far below the 0.05 ratio limb, and POL-GEN-01 forbids using any other profile field - or the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags - for this test. The clause's consult trigger is not met on materiality either: even on the whole-trace reading the excess is 27.3% and 4.80 km, whereas a MATERIAL deviation requires more than 50% or more than 8.0 km.

Separately from any exoneration, the compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is engaged on the artifacts' own figures: the fare_breakdown billed the rider for distance_charged_km of 20.0 (weight 1.0) while the gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 22.4, a shortfall of 2.4 unbilled kilometres, above the 1.0 km threshold. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 and within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. Disclosure: the 22.4 km figure is carried by EV-GPS-00112, which is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so this limb is asserted on a down-weighted trace and is worth what that discount says it is worth.

On the rider's PLQ request the driver does not press an exoneration he cannot corroborate. The chat log shows the rider's request in MSG-00112-001, carrying a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the driver's 'ok can' in MSG-00112-002 - so POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are met - but the trace's nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m away (fix 158, 18:45:00), well outside the 200 m corroboration radius POL-RD-04 sets. The corroboration limb cannot be run on this record, no distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded, and POL-RD-14 directs that the instruction was made and did not reduce the measured excess. What does not follow is any refund: no fare line charges a stop fee or a missed-stop fee, and in any event the distance-and-time lines recompute to zero, so the missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing. Disclosure: the 512.35 m figure comes from EV-GPS-00112, IMPAIRED at 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The uncorroborated detour request is not an escalation trigger. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14 to the case where the trace corroborates the rider's instruction in part, so that the excess attributable to it cannot be separated from the rest. Here the trace corroborates nothing about the waypoint, and a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other - that is a failed corroboration under POL-RD-04, not two contradictory bodies of comparable evidence. POL-RD-14 directs that the deviation be decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured, which also disposes of POL-GEN-07: a clause of the policy in force does license an outcome on these facts, so no residual-principles escalation is open.

No mandatory escalation trigger fires on the timestamp point either. POL-RD-10(4) asks whether pickup or dropoff timestamps on two admitted artifacts disagree by more than 10 minutes. The pickup and dropoff events themselves align: the trip record's arrival at the pickup, 18:17:50, against the trace's first fix at 18:18:40 - 50 seconds; and the record's ended_at 18:52:20 against the trace's last fix at 18:52:12 - 8 seconds. What diverges is the meter start (18:32:10) and the trace's first fix, i.e. the pre-start segment; that is the schema-level CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT the pre-pass has already priced at weight 0.4 under POL-GEN-02, and it does not meet POL-RD-07(a) to (c) at all - the trace has no gaps, a longest gap of 0 seconds and a 10 second sampling interval against a 30 second limb - so it carries POL-GEN-02 consequences only and does not engage POL-RD-07's or POL-RD-10(3)'s consequences. Disclosure: both artifacts cited are IMPAIRED at 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The facts that decide this dispute are carried by the clean artifact. What decides it is what was charged and what the fare model yields for the booked optimal route, and those figures sit on EV-FARE-00112, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issues and whose line items 'reconcile to the cent'. The 0.4 discount sits on the trace and the trip record and goes to the measured actual distance, not to any charged line or to the booking-time optimal estimate. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cap follows the artifacts that carry the deciding fact, and the deciding fact here is carried at 1.0.

ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-00112-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: My client did ask for the Paya Lebar Quarter stop and the driver agreed in terms ('ok can', MSG-00112-002, sent 18:33:30). But a rider instruction exonerates distance only if the trace corroborates it: POL-RD-04 requires the vehicle to pass within 200 m of chat_message.waypoint_hint, resolved here to VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER. It never did — the nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m away (fix index 158, at 18:45:00) against the 200 m threshold. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate caused nothing: no distance is excluded and the excess stands as measured. EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4) and I disclose it; the waypoint distances are its own derived field.

The driver says he 'did make the PLQ stop... waited about four minutes there'. His device says otherwise: the closest the vehicle comes to the PLQ waypoint is 512 m and the trace shows no dwell there, so his account of compliance fails on the very artifact that would have proved it. On POL-RD-14 the instruction is found and not corroborated, and under POL-RD-08 a driver assertion that points to no supporting artifact discharges nothing. What the trace does prove is my client's grievance — she asked for the stop and the vehicle never went near it. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4).

The two admitted records disagree about when this trip began by more than the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4): EV-TRIP-00112's started_at is 18:32:10, while EV-GPS-00112's first fix is at 18:18:40 — 13 minutes 30 seconds earlier — and 2.38 km of trace falls inside a period the trip record says had not started. The disagreement is outcome-determinative: over the whole trace the excess is 27.27% and the POL-RD-01 gate is cleared; measured from started_at only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 13.8%, below the gate. POL-RD-10 makes escalation terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it, which is the only course that does not leave my client paying a charge this record cannot justify. What would resolve it is a record-type item: the device event log for DRV-03187 distinguishing a late meter start from the tail of a previous job, or a corrected trip start. Both cited artifacts are IMPAIRED, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4, which I disclose.

Independently of POL-RD-10(4), no merits ruling can be issued at or above the platform's 0.70 confidence floor. The fact this dispute turns on — the excess — is carried by EV-GPS-00112 (22.40 km driven) and EV-TRIP-00112 (17.60 km optimal), each at weight_multiplier 0.4 on the pre-pass. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence may not exceed the weight_multiplier of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, which here is 0.4, so POL-RD-10(1) is engaged and the case goes to a human reviewer with the amount held. Both cited artifacts are IMPAIRED with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and I disclose that.

POL-RD-01 measures the excess as the length of the gps_trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and it is the trace, not the rounded meter copy, that governs. On this trip the recorded pickup event is the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10, while the trace runs from 18:18:40 to 18:52:12, so 2.38 km of the trace lies before the trip the platform recorded. On the assessor's own alignment figures for that artifact the segment actually driven is 20.02 km, an excess of 2.42 km, or 13.8% of the 17.6 km booked optimal - under the 20% limb of POL-RD-01. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass; the percentage limb fails, so the excess is not established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The whole-trace figures of 4.80 km and 27.3% (derived.deviation) are an artefact of counting that 2.38 km head, which is exactly why the pre-pass records that the interpretation moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

Even if the tribunal takes the whole trace as the measured trip and holds the deviation established, POL-RD-02 returns nothing to the rider. The fare model is METERED, so the recomputation runs on this trip's own figures: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP, tolls, surcharges, waiting fee and promo = 25.64, against a charged_total of 25.26. Refund = charged_total - recomputed_fare = -0.38, floored at zero; a refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis. The fare_breakdown's own derived money block carries the same result (recomputed_fare 25.6400, refund payable 0.00, below_de_minimis true). The booked optimal figures are the booking-time estimate carried on that money block; the CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT flagged on EV-TRIP-00112 (IMPAIRED, 0.4) goes to the measured actual distance, not to the booking-time optimal route or to any charged line. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge standing exactly as it is.

The reason the recomputation exceeds what was charged is visible line by line, and it is the rider's own time, not the driver's distance, that is the source. The optimal route - PIE westbound then ECP - is 17.6 km but 28.0 minutes, while the rider was charged for 20.2 minutes. The optimal-route time charge is 7.84 (28.0 x 0.28) against the 5.66 actually billed (20.2 x 0.28); that single line more than offsets the 1.80 of extra distance charge (20.0 km x 0.75 = 15.00 against 17.6 km x 0.75 = 13.20). Net of the two, the rider paid 0.38 LESS than the fare model says the optimal route would have cost.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to add on top of a zero distance-and-time refund. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll, no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount; erp_gantries is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00. No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. POL-RD-09 therefore has nothing to correct on this trip and the billing-integrity limb of POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral do not apply. The clause's test runs on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d: this driver carries 1 flag over 296 completed trips in the trailing 90 days. That is below the 3-flag limb and far below the 0.05 ratio limb, and POL-GEN-01 forbids using any other profile field - or the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags - for this test. The clause's consult trigger is not met on materiality either: even on the whole-trace reading the excess is 27.3% and 4.80 km, whereas a MATERIAL deviation requires more than 50% or more than 8.0 km.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: Separately from any exoneration, the compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is engaged on the artifacts' own figures: the fare_breakdown billed the rider for distance_charged_km of 20.0 (weight 1.0) while the gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 22.4, a shortfall of 2.4 unbilled kilometres, above the 1.0 km threshold. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 and within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. Disclosure: the 22.4 km figure is carried by EV-GPS-00112, which is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so this limb is asserted on a down-weighted trace and is worth what that discount says it is worth.

On the rider's PLQ request the driver does not press an exoneration he cannot corroborate. The chat log shows the rider's request in MSG-00112-001, carrying a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the driver's 'ok can' in MSG-00112-002 - so POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are met - but the trace's nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m away (fix 158, 18:45:00), well outside the 200 m corroboration radius POL-RD-04 sets. The corroboration limb cannot be run on this record, no distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded, and POL-RD-14 directs that the instruction was made and did not reduce the measured excess. What does not follow is any refund: no fare line charges a stop fee or a missed-stop fee, and in any event the distance-and-time lines recompute to zero, so the missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing. Disclosure: the 512.35 m figure comes from EV-GPS-00112, IMPAIRED at 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The uncorroborated detour request is not an escalation trigger. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14 to the case where the trace corroborates the rider's instruction in part, so that the excess attributable to it cannot be separated from the rest. Here the trace corroborates nothing about the waypoint, and a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other - that is a failed corroboration under POL-RD-04, not two contradictory bodies of comparable evidence. POL-RD-14 directs that the deviation be decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured, which also disposes of POL-GEN-07: a clause of the policy in force does license an outcome on these facts, so no residual-principles escalation is open.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00112 at weight_multiplier 0.4 but does not name its issue code(s): CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT

ledger.claim: No mandatory escalation trigger fires on the timestamp point either. POL-RD-10(4) asks whether pickup or dropoff timestamps on two admitted artifacts disagree by more than 10 minutes. The pickup and dropoff events themselves align: the trip record's arrival at the pickup, 18:17:50, against the trace's first fix at 18:18:40 - 50 seconds; and the record's ended_at 18:52:20 against the trace's last fix at 18:52:12 - 8 seconds. What diverges is the meter start (18:32:10) and the trace's first fix, i.e. the pre-start segment; that is the schema-level CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT the pre-pass has already priced at weight 0.4 under POL-GEN-02, and it does not meet POL-RD-07(a) to (c) at all - the trace has no gaps, a longest gap of 0 seconds and a 10 second sampling interval against a 30 second limb - so it carries POL-GEN-02 consequences only and does not engage POL-RD-07's or POL-RD-10(3)'s consequences. Disclosure: both artifacts cited are IMPAIRED at 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The facts that decide this dispute are carried by the clean artifact. What decides it is what was charged and what the fare model yields for the booked optimal route, and those figures sit on EV-FARE-00112, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issues and whose line items 'reconcile to the cent'. The 0.4 discount sits on the trace and the trip record and goes to the measured actual distance, not to any charged line or to the booking-time optimal estimate. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cap follows the artifacts that carry the deciding fact, and the deciding fact here is carried at 1.0.
